level_1: With guidance, recognizes signs and symptoms of inborn errors of metabolism and identifies when further testing is needed

Develops and implements an initial management plan for complex or rare patient presentations of inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency, carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase deficiency)
level_2: Selects and orders diagnostic tests and develops a rudimentary management plan for initial evaluation or implements the existing management plan
Synthesizes the clinical context and pattern of laboratory results to identify the likelihood of a complex or rare inborn error of metabolism
level_3: Independently recognizes signs and symptoms of inborn errors of metabolism and identifies when further testing is needed
Anticipates and creates contingency plan for an acute response and develops an acute secondary plan
level_4: Develops and implements an initial management plan for common patient presentations of inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., organic aciduria, urea cycle)
Leads development of institutional protocols for diagnosis and management of inborn errors of metabolism
level_5: Synthesizes the clinical context and pattern of laboratory results to identify the likelihood of a common inborn error of metabolism

level_1: Takes a comprehensive genetic history for a patient with pertinent positive and negative findings; integrates the history with other data to develop a differential diagnosis
Provides routine disease- specific surveillance
Guides a patient through shared decision making on novel or high-risk therapies; coordinates implementation of these therapies
level_2: Implements dietary and medical therapy for patients with a common inborn error of metabolism (e.g., carnitine uptake defect, medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, dietary therapy for phenylketonuria (PKU))
Takes a disease-specific history for a patient with a complex inborn error of metabolism with multisystemic manifestations (e.g., Hunter syndrome)
Anticipates and creates contingency plans for highly pleotropic inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., mucopolysaccharidosis
level_3: Provides symptomatic and supportive care to patients
Identifies a patient who, based on natural history, is a candidate for disease modifying therapy (e.g., solid organ transplant, enzyme replacement therapy, cell-based therapy)
I)
level_4: Takes an inborn error of metabolism focused history for a patient with an established common inborn error of metabolism (e.g., PKU)
Provides ongoing comprehensive surveillance of disease progression and care coordination
Implements a clinical trial to improve management of patients with an inborn error of metabolism
level_5: Synthesizes clinical and laboratory data to optimize complex dietary and medical therapy (e.g., urea cycle disorders)
Efficiently takes a nuanced disease- specific history for a patient with an inborn error of metabolism
Implements a multi- disciplinary clinic for care of patients with an inborn error of metabolism

level_1: Applies published (state or national) protocols to obtain follow-up testing based on initial newborn screen results
Makes appropriate decisions about urgency of implementation of management based on initial clinical history
level_2: Applies published (state or national) protocols for initial management based on the initial newborn screen result
Integrates data from multiple sources to arrive at an accurate diagnosis for the patient
level_3: Generates a differential diagnosis based on newborn screen results that includes diagnoses other than inherited metabolic diseases
Develops a plan for management of a patient with incidental findings or results that indicate concern for a disease that is not intended to be identified with newborn screening
level_4: Develops a continuing management plan when initial testing is inconclusive
Participates in state, regional, or national newborn screening program policy development or evaluation projects
level_5: Applies published protocols for diagnosis with modifications to account for patient specific factors

level_1: Describes biochemical pathways and principles underpinning diagnosis and therapy for categories of inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., protein restriction, cofactor therapy, pathway modifying medications)
level_2: Describes how manipulation of biochemical pathways through various therapeutic modalities (diet, medications, etc.) can be employed for management of specific inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency versus argininosuccinate lyase deficiency; cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency versus cobalamin C disease)
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the interconnectedness of biochemical pathways and employs these concepts in diagnosis and management
level_4: Integrates knowledge of the complex nature of biochemical pathways to prioritize and employ the range of therapeutic options for a patient, based upon an individual’s clinical and biochemical response to therapy
level_5: Expands understanding of underlying biochemical basis of inborn errors of metabolism through publication of new knowledge that impacts the diagnosis or treatment of a disease or category of inborn errors of metabolism

level_1: Describes the technology and use of diagnostic testing for inborn errors of metabolism
Identifies best methods for diagnosis and subsequent laboratory monitoring for common inborn errors of metabolism
Integrates data from multiple sources to identify how likely an individual newborn screening test is a true positive
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the differences between newborn screening and diagnostic testing
Interprets complex metabolic testing (e.g., very long chain fatty acids) for inborn errors of metabolism
Develops polices or practice guidelines for diagnostic testing of inborn errors of metabolism
level_3: Identifies possible methods for diagnosis and subsequent laboratory monitoring for inborn errors of metabolism
Demonstrates knowledge of positive predictive values of newborn screening tests and tools for improved discrimination of positive and negative results
Participates in new assay development or gene discovery
level_4: Interprets common metabolic testing (e.g., plasma amino acids) for inborn errors of metabolism
Identifies best methods for diagnosis and subsequent laboratory monitoring for complex inborn errors of metabolism
Contributes to generalizable medical knowledge of newborn screening tests
level_5: Describes causes of false positive/negative rates and how these factors can impact newborn screening test interpretation
Integrates results of metabolic and genomic testing to arrive at a diagnosis

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local (institutional) quality improvement initiatives
Independently discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local (institutional) quality improvement initiatives
Mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community (state/federal) level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
Models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand- offs within and across health care delivery systems including outpatient settings, referrals, and testing
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations including advocating for a patient’s genetic testing coverage
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of quality improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams, including non-physician patient caregivers
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties including referrals and testing
Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs at the state or federal level

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)

Advocates for patient care needs (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources) with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model, including genetic testing through research
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., access to genetic testing and treatments, testing advocacy)
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice
level_3: Identifies basic knowledge for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding, financial, personnel)
Engages with patients in shared decision making, often informed by each patient’s payment models
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transition of care
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model (e.g., insurance type) and access to genetic testing or formula
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
Educates others to prepare them for transition to practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values to take care of a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Mentors others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Mentors others on reflective practice
level_2: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Seeks performance data consistently with adaptability and humility
Facilitates the design and implementing learning plans for others
level_3: Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Develops evaluations or education resources/tools for learners
level_4: Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability and humility
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and when necessary, improves it
Participates in the development of courses for the education of students or other physicians
level_5: Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Models seeking performance data with adaptability and humility

level_1: Demonstrates compassion, sensitivity, honesty, integrity, and identifies potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Identifies different types of conflicts of interest, knows guidelines for interactions with vendors
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care
Demonstrates compassion, sensitivity, honesty, and integrity in complex/stressful situations
Demonstrates consistently professional behavior regarding conflicts of interest relevant to presentations, publishing, consulting, and service
level_3: Demonstrates basic knowledge of conflict of interest
Recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_4: Demonstrates compassion, sensitivity, honesty, integrity, and takes responsibility for own professionalism lapses
Identifies resources for managing and resolving conflicts of interest
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_5: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Demonstrates compassion, sensitivity, honesty, integrity, and serves as a role model to others

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Demonstrates a professional appearance, daily demeanor, and conduct
Promotes professional appearance, demeanor, and conduct in their peers and associates
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
Volunteers to improve and takes ownership of system outcomes
level_3: Recognizes the role of appearance, daily demeanor and conduct in the role of a professional
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_4: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Sets a standard for appearance, daily demeanor, and conduct as a professional
level_5: Recognizes situations that may impact his/her own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Recognizes and addresses situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
With assistance, proposes a plan to remediate or improve limits in the knowledge/ skills of self or team
level_2: Recognizes limits in the knowledge/skills of self or team, with assistance
Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_3: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to remediate or improve limits in the knowledge/skills of self or team
level_4: Independently recognizes limits in the knowledge/ skills of self or team and demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors
Coaches others when emotional responses or limitations in knowledge/skills do not meet professional expectations
level_5: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being

level_1: Uses language and nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Organizes and initiates communication with patient/family by introducing stakeholders, setting the agenda, clarifying expectations, and verifying understanding of the clinical situation
Recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication while accurately communicating own role within the health care system
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters
Uses shared decision making to align patient/family values, goals, and preferences with treatment options to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Identifies the need to adjust communication strategies based on assessment of patient/family expectations and understanding of their health status and treatment options
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information, elicits patient/family values, goals, and preferences, and acknowledges uncertainty and conflict
Models self-awareness practice while identifying teaching a contextual approach to minimize communication barriers
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication
Establishes therapeutic relationships, with attention to patient/family concerns and context, regardless of complexity
Models shared decision making in patient/family communication including those with a high degree of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Clearly and concisely requests a consultation
Uses active listening to adapt communication style to fit team needs
Leads interactions between the primary care and metabolic team regarding rationale for recommendations
level_2: Clearly and concisely responds to a consultation request
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
Provides constructive feedback on active listening to health care team members
level_3: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Provides information to the primary care team regarding rationale for recommendations
Models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_4: Checks own understanding of consultant recommendations
Models active listening to other health care team members
level_5: Checks requestor’s understanding of recommendations when providing consultation
Leads an interprofessional metabolic team to optimize patient care

level_1: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Achieves written or verbal communication (e.g., patient notes, email) that serves as an example for others to follow
level_2: Uses documentation shortcuts accurately, appropriately and in a timely manner
Provides feedback to more junior learners on reporting diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
level_3: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Mentors more junior learners in written and verbal communication
level_4: Appropriately selects direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) forms of communication based on context
Models feedback to improve others’ written communication
level_5: Communicates clearly, concisely, timely, and in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
